- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion; if 3–5 day moving average is below 70, forecast should not drop below 65 unless sentiment confirms strong bearish shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ true values before applying sentiment adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.27 spikes, model tends to overcorrect; apply 10–15% dampening to forecast if sentiment > 0.25 for 2+ consecutive days.
